independence_statement: Created before opening the existing worth-trip batch files, candidate spot records, image-review-001.json or progress.md. Only candidate names/countries from the assignment were used.
method_limits: No authorized full cloud-database access was available.
Coordinates from search/geocoding are not treated as exact launch coordinates unless an official or operator source identifies the access point.
Pexels and Unsplash API credentials were unavailable; public indexed results were checked, but absence of a result does not mean absence of an image.
Wikimedia/Openverse title matches are candidates only. A name match without coordinates or unmistakable landmarks is not geo-verification.
Fields not positively supported remain open; not found is never interpreted as not present.

spots.name: Domburg Noordduine

identity.separate_subspot: Likely a named beach sector north-west of Domburg; boundary against Domburg Badstrand/Westkapelle requires local map confirmation.

entry.note: No independent exact launch point established.

conditions.water: North Sea beach break; exposed surf
conditions.tide_current: Open; exposed North Sea conditions and currents require caution.

spots.access_rules: Municipal rules identify the Noordduine sector as an exception zone for wind/surf/kite activities, but July-August surfing restrictions near the Noordduine pavilion and current on-site zoning must be checked.

trip_value.reason: Strong Zeeland surf context, but the named sector is insufficiently separated from the wider Domburg/Westkapelle destination.

image_review.note: Openverse exact-name results were non-commercial/no-derivatives and too small; no independently geo-verified hero found.

spots.name: Vrouwenpolder

identity.separate_subspot: North Sea kite zone and Veerse Meer windsurf/wing area are distinct launches and should not be collapsed into one coordinate.

entry.note: At least two activity areas; exact launch must identify North Sea versus Veerse Meer.

conditions.water: North Sea waves plus calmer Veerse Meer
conditions.tide_current: Kite lagoon effect reported mainly at high/spring tide; Veerse Meer is a separate flat-water setting.

spots.access_rules: Marked kite zone with signs/buoys in season; use only permitted side of buoys. Municipal exception zone exists. Paid parking; local NKV information point and school.

trip_value.reason: Two complementary water settings, broad sport support and established infrastructure make it a credible Zeeland trip anchor.

image_review.note: Commons CC BY-SA beach images and an exact Breezand Unsplash kite image exist. Exact launch/landmark verification and full-resolution check are still required before hero use.

spots.name: Chia – Su Giudeu

identity.separate_subspot: Su Giudeu is one beach within the wider Chia coast; Cala Cipolla and Porto Campana are not aliases.

entry.note: OpenStreetMap beach point, not a verified rigging/launch point.

conditions.water: Mediterranean beach with wave conditions mainly in stronger weather
conditions.tide_current: Currents and wave action reported; no quantified primary evidence.

spots.access_rules: No confirmed public kite corridor for 2026. Peak-season beach launching is reported as unavailable due to swimmers; paid boat launch may be required. Dunes may not be crossed and wild camping is prohibited.

trip_value.reason: Scenic and potentially strong wave-kite conditions, but access/rules are too restrictive and insufficiently primary-sourced for a confident travel recommendation.

spots.name: Perranporth

identity.separate_subspot: Joins Perran Sands at low tide; should not be treated as identical to the entire combined beach.

entry.note: Geocode resolves to surf school/access, not a universal launch.

conditions.tide_current: Large tidal beach; rip-current specifics not independently confirmed here.

spots.access_rules: RNLI flags/zones and lifeguard instructions apply; busy family beach. Large seafront parking, cafes and multiple surf schools.

trip_value.reason: Established Cornish surf destination with long beach, lessons and good access; travel value is surfing-led.

image_review.note: Commons has a CC BY 4.0 image explicitly titled Perranporth beach waves; resolution/composition needs hero review.

spots.name: Neeltje Jans

identity.separate_subspot: Artificial island has multiple shores; the permitted kite/wind sector must be named and pinned separately from the visitor attraction.

entry.note: Geocoder returned Speelstrand; not proven to be the launch.

conditions.tide_current: Tidal/current risk likely material but not sufficiently quantified in independent sources.

spots.access_rules: Municipal exception zone runs from Roompotsluis side to De Slufter crossing. Site is within National Park Oosterschelde/Voordelta context; current signage controls exact use.

trip_value.reason: Distinctive Delta Works setting and exposed conditions, but launch/current details need strong local verification.

image_review.note: Commons/Unsplash images verify Neeltje Jans island/engineering landscape but not the launch; suitable only as regional gallery until launch landmarks are confirmed.

spots.name: Gwithian Towans

identity.separate_subspot: Connected to Godrevy/Hayle Towans at low tide but remains a distinct access and named beach.

entry.note: Geocode is a bus stop/access proxy, not the launch.

conditions.tide_current: Serious rip currents documented; beach joins neighbouring sands at low tide.

spots.access_rules: Seasonal activity zoning sends wind/kite sports south of the marked restricted area and outside bathing/surf zones. Dune code prohibits vehicles, fires, BBQs and overnight camping.

trip_value.reason: Consistent surf, broad skill range and a highly scenic St Ives Bay setting support a surf-led trip.

image_review.note: Commons exact-location CC BY-SA images exist, including lifeguard/access landmarks; hero suitability depends on resolution and composition.

spots.name: Sennen Cove

identity.separate_subspot: Gwynver is a neighbouring quieter surf access, not an alias.

entry.note: Beach point; access varies with flags and tide.

conditions.water: Atlantic beach break with sometimes large rollers
conditions.tide_current: RNLI flags move with tidal conditions; current detail remains open.

spots.access_rules: Follow RNLI flags; lifeguarded April/early season through October in published 2026 schedule context. Multiple car parks, year-round bus, surf school/hire and food.

trip_value.reason: Iconic far-west Cornwall setting and established surfing infrastructure justify travel value.

image_review.note: Commons exact-location images exist but sampled results are street/coastal-path or historical views, not a strong verified surf hero.

spots.name: Rossnowlagh

identity.separate_subspot: Large beach with multiple accesses; not one precise launch.

entry.note: Village geocode (54.5543518, -8.2097755) is not the beach access.

conditions.tide_current: Winter surf can be large; exact rip/tide behaviour remains open.

spots.access_rules: Summer lifeguards and flag system. Beach access/vehicle practices must follow current local signs. Several surf schools and a kite school operate locally.

image_review.note: Several Commons CC BY-SA files explicitly show Rossnowlagh Beach; assess dimensions/composition before hero selection.
